subtitle: The common rotating interface
description: A 400 mm disc and detachable flanged hub define a shared prototype interface. The drum variant appears in the drum-brake package. This is a geometry study, not a speed-rated rotor.
targets: Shaft, balance and thermal assessment required
decisions: Use a detachable hub to replace the friction disc without replacing the shaft interface.
Begin with machined steel for prototype traceability; evaluate a cast-iron friction variant only through paired friction and thermal tests.
Use one six-hole interface across the first disc concepts; bolt preload and joint slip capacity remain to be sized.
materials: Disc: C45 normalized steel candidate; friction compound must be qualified with this surface.
Hub: 42CrMo4 quenched-and-tempered candidate; property certificate must correspond to actual section size.
risks: Disc-to-hub torque transfer, bolt preload and fatigue are not yet established.
No keyway or locking element is released; the 50 mm bore is an interface placeholder.
Thermal coning, hot runout, balance and overspeed remain unverified.
steps: Inspect disc and hub identification, bore and interface faces.
Locate disc on the hub spigot; align six through holes.
Fit the specified through-bolts, washers and nuts after joint design is approved.
Measure assembled runout and balance before guarded testing.
validation: Thermal transient model with moving pad heat flux and measured heat partition.
Bolted joint slip, bearing, hub torsion and rotational stress calculations.
Guarded speed, runout, balance and repeated stop tests.
hypotheses: Time disc replacement versus a documented integral-hub baseline with the same shaft access.
Count unique components across the disc-brake concepts; this is not a competitor advantage claim.
sensors: Reserve non-contact runout measurement access and a temperature observation window.
